author: nero_eth
content: One thing to consider, which might apply more to the payload than to the bid, if blacklisted traffic isn't throttled at the p2p, then, even though it will be rejected locally, it's a DoS.

author: vladimir_ea
content:
DoS would entail repeated invalid payloads / missing payloads would it not? a single missed block is not considered DoS at the moment?

It seems like DoS protection could be handled in protocol by taxing builder collateral, for example, making it non-viable economically. It seems like this is actually already in place with the builder-must-pay-trustless payment in the event of a missing payload. 

So I wonder why this additional banning is required?

That leave trusted payment path as a possible DoS path - but it seems unlikely that any builder will remain trusted for long who does such a thing.

author: nero_eth
content: I'd consider it a DoS attack as soon as an attacker could cause some significant work at the victim, if the slot is missed or not is how successful the attack is (same for drop in participation, missed attestations, nodes forking off, etc). Not talking about general DoS prevention here but more gaps in the client implementations (missing dedups, early propagation) might lead to those nodes acting as an accelerator wrt DoS.

author: vladimir_ea
content: the discussion about circuit breakers has been only about banning builders who send winning bids and then do not produce a valid payload on time - this can be prevented economically it seems to me.

author: vladimir_ea
content: (and the mechanism is already in place to do so)

author: vladimir_ea
content: what are the DoS scenarios you are thinking of?

author: vladimir_ea
content: I belive that each builder is allowed only one bid per slot over p2p - so that seems easy enough to detect

author: nero_eth
content: E.g. not producing a valid payload in time could mean that builder is winning multiple slots in a row to then release all the payloads at once. If there are missing dedups, then one could release thousands of payloads per slot into an entirely different slot, DoSing attesters and of the proposers.

author: vladimir_ea
content:
you don't need to be a builder to send invalid payloads. you also do not need to be a specific builder to include that builder's index in some made-up payload. anyone can flood p2p with invalid payloads - this is normally handled by p2p downscoring and banning connections. gossip messages are deduped. such mechanisms already exist.

there is at most one valid payload per slot identified by builder index and signed with their key.

it is possible that some registered builder will genrate 1000s of invalid payloads and sign them with their real keys - not sure why, but its possible - but connections forwarding such messages would soon be dropped. 

But again, the gossip spec says that invalid messages should not be forwarded and that connects are downscored and soon banned for sending invalid messages.

author: vladimir_ea
content: winning multiple slots in a row and then releasing payloads: they would pay for every payload not delivered on time. late payloads are not considered so can be dropped early.

author: nero_eth
content: Let's keep the DoS-related discussions in <#892088344438255616>

author: vladimir_ea
content: I actually see no justification for this out-of-protocol builder banning that is being suggested. Would be good if someone could outline why is it required and why the pay-on-missing penalty is not considered sufficient.

author: 0xunclebill
content: an unpatched builder bug could result in multiple missed slots. weve seen this already happen on mainnet before. in the worse case these can cause the global circuit breaker to trip which is a bad scenario for everyone. epbs gives us more granular control on circuit breakers. ideally we never have to trigger a global circuit breaker, and instead temporarily ban individual buggy builders

author: vladimir_ea
content: and every missed slot costs such a builder their collateral, until they stop or they have none left. 'buggy' prposers that casue missed slots are not banned, or even penalised.

author: vladimir_ea
content: is it correct to infer from a single missed payload that a builder is buggy and should therefore be banned?

author: vladimir_ea
content: it is not inferred that a proposer is buggy if they are offline for a slot

author: 0xunclebill
content: the big builders build a vast majority of blocks. a proposer proposes one block once a year maybe? weve already seen this on mainnet. a buggy builder caused multiple missed slots. this triggers the global circuit breaker. we revert to lcoal block building for x amount of time. thats bad because most transactions these days are submitted privately. so only txs in the public mempool are included while the circuit breaker is triggered. thats a liveness issue

author: 0xunclebill
content: if you're arguing about how harsh the circuit breaker penalties need to be, sure that can be discussed

author: 0xunclebill
content: but there is plenty of justification for a more granular  circuit breaker imo

author: vladimir_ea
content:
the circuit breaker as proposed is also: 1 missed payload = builder banned; 1 missed payload via relay = all builders that ever submitted via that relay banned. not just the scenario you describe

an argument there was it is to 'incentivize' not missing payloads - but I am not sure that holds; there are many reasons outwith a builders control that might result in a missed slot, e.g. a service provider outage, or simply receiving attestations late or not at all.

i can see that a global circuit breaker in the event of multiple consecutive missed or invalid payloads can be justified, but these individual builder / relay bans seem like over reach,

author: 0xunclebill
content: the global circuit breaker is the situation we want to avoid. i dont think individual builder bans are overreach , esp if they can help prevent the worse scenario of a temporary global builder ban.

author: 0xunclebill
content: maybe a immediate temp ban for one missed payload is too harsh, i dont know. all im saying is the individual circuit breaker is a good thing for the health of the network

author: vladimir_ea
content: do you think it is correct to infer that a builder is a threat to the health of the network if a single payload is missed?

author: vladimir_ea
content: and why is the economic incentive insufficient in this case?

author: 0xunclebill
content: assuming a healthy network going along the happy path, yeah. i think we need to be careful in the non happy path cases

author: 0xunclebill
content: because weve seen this play out on mainnet before. weve seen the global circuit breaker trigger.

author: vladimir_ea
content: 'yeah' as in it is correct to infer that? do you not think there may be many reason outside a builders control for missing a payload?

author: vladimir_ea
content: lets say, for example, that there is a service provider outage - you would blame a builder that had bid before the outage but was unable to release the payload ?

author: 0xunclebill
content: its unlucky and an unlikely scenario. but sure the builder will be penalized. in that scenario their infra is down anyways so a 1 epoch ban or w/e doesnt seem like that big of a deal?

author: vladimir_ea
content: but what exactly is the point of the ban in such a scenario? or any scenario where a single payload is missed? how do you conclude that the netwrok is threatened? its a false inference,

author: vladimir_ea
content: perhaps its not a big deal to the builder (disagree), but its not clear what the benefit is to anyone

author: 0xunclebill
content: one payload missed isnt a big deal, but chain a few together and now we have to trigger the global circuit breaker

author: 0xunclebill
content:
the point of the ban is to ensure that we dont have to trigger the global circuit breaker in the situation where one or two popular builders/relays has a bug. 

anyways i think ive made my position clear, i dont want to just keep repeating myself

author: vladimir_ea
content: i see: single missed payload, ban just in case it leads to more missed payloads, its not a big deal anyway.
